_: Lining oral mucosa of the cheek (buccal) and inner lip (labial): non-keratinised stratified squamous epithelium over a loose lamina propria and submucosa, always wet with a saliva film in life. Mechanics are for adult tissue; the tensile values come from Thiel-embalmed elderly donors (stiffer, high-strain region), the in vivo indentation value is the low-strain figure a contact solver should use. The hard palate (masticatory mucosa) is given as a variant inside the values. Materials research lane, mouth group, 2026-11-07.

alpha.src: JACQ13 not a gloss source: a moist non-keratinised epithelium is smoother than skin (skin.body 0.35, Donner 2008); 0.25 E for the tissue under its film; in life the saliva coat (states.wet, the default) sets the highlight

n.src: JACQ13 soft tissue 1.36-1.40; no keratin layer (stratum corneum 1.47-1.55 absent)

thickness_um.src: ASSY23 median film inside cheek 44.0 (IQR 34.8-58.5) um (via MTT D19); inner lip not measured, cheek value used (E for the lip)

translucency.v: high: no keratin or melanin layer to speak of, so the lamina propria's blood shows; redder than skin
translucency.src: JACQ13 general tissue optics; colour values not found

colour_Lab.src: not found: no instrument L*a*b* for buccal or labial mucosa retrieved (MTT section 11 lists it missing too); gingiva HO15 L* 52.9 a* 23.3 b* 14.9 is keratinised and paler, so mucosa is expected redder

wet_gloss.v: sharp specular from the saliva film (n 1.335) over a soft diffuse red base; the film is 30-70 um, thick enough to smooth fine relief
wet_gloss.src: from ASSY23 film thickness and WATER n

static.src: not found: no in vivo human buccal mucosa coefficient retrieved

kinetic.src: BONGAERTS07 PDMS with whole saliva boundary mu ~0.02 and dried saliva 2-3 (model surfaces); porcine tongue with artificial saliva minimum ~0.35 (thesis, via search); RANC06 a salivary layer lowers mucosal friction x1.6; PRINZ07 mucosa-on-mucosa mu falls with load (0.34-2.2 N) and speed. The bracket is the spread of model systems, not a measured buccal value

friction.counterface: PDMS model surfaces and porcine/piglet tongue; see pairs/mouth.json

surface_energy_mJ_m2.src: not found for human buccal mucosa; RANC06 tongue mucosa weakly polar and hydrophobic-leaning without saliva, hydrophilic once coated

tack.v: mucoadhesive: mucin (MUC5B) layer bonds to hydrophilic polymers; wet tissue against itself shows little tack because the saliva film lubricates (work of adhesion is reported per formulation in uJ/cm2, not as a tissue constant)
tack.src: mucoadhesion literature (tensile detachment on porcine buccal mucosa) gives formulation-dependent values only; ASSY23 MUC5B at all intra-oral sites

restitution.src: not found; a hydrated viscoelastic soft tissue: treat as heavily damped (deform.viscoelastic)

water_contact_angle_deg.src: ANDABLO20 pig tongue static ~77 deg as a mucosal proxy; RANC06 the salivary layer makes the mucosa more hydrophilic (values not retrieved)

water_absorption.v: saturated in life; the epithelium is permeable (non-keratinised)

collision_thickness_mm.src: ASSY23 saliva film inside the cheek 44 um: the gap a solver keeps is the film

contact_stiffness_kPa_per_mm.src: E / thickness: in vivo 80 kPa (SAWADA11) over ~3 mm epithelium + lamina propria + submucosa (thickness E)

contact_damping_ratio.src: hydrated soft tissue contacts are heavily damped; muscle 0.14-0.42 (MUSCLE damping_ratio); 0.3 a middle value

response_time_ms.src: soft-tissue contact pulse: a few shear-wave transits of the 3 mm layer (D ~1.2 ms each at 5 m/s) lengthened by damping

damping_ratio.src: hydrated soft tissue contacts are heavily damped; muscle 0.14-0.42 (MUSCLE damping_ratio); 0.3 a middle value

E_kPa.src: not separated from the whole; in vivo whole value SAWADA11 used

compressible_to_fraction.src: near-incompressible (hydrated epithelium): a layer thins only by flowing sideways; 0.95 of thickness under ordinary contact, more under sustained load

thickness_mm.src: not measured; cheek wall total ~10 mm with muscle and fat

compressible_to_fraction.src: near-incompressible (loose connective tissue): a layer thins only by flowing sideways; 0.95 of thickness under ordinary contact, more under sustained load

compliance_layers.name: buccinator muscle (free wall: no bone behind the cheek; the inner lip lies on teeth)

compressible_to_fraction.src: near-incompressible (muscle): a layer thins only by flowing sideways; 0.95 of thickness under ordinary contact, more under sustained load

deform.model_note: neo-Hookean base with a long relaxation; incompressible

density_kg_m3.src: soft tissue; MUSCLE 1060, skin 1090 bracket it; not measured for mucosa

E_kPa.src: SAWADA11 in vivo initial modulus 8.0e-5 GPa (= 80 kPa); CHOI20 Thiel buccal 8.33 +- 5.78 MPa, hard palate 18.13 +- 4.51 MPa (uniaxial tension, high-strain region). The in vivo value is the low-strain contact stiffness

E_kPa_literature_range.src: KYDD67 tensile moduli 0.91-11.12 MPa; other studies 0.37-5.80 MPa (Tanaka 1973, Inoue 1985, Nakashima 1975 as quoted in CHOI20)

shear_kPa.src: G = E/(2(1+nu)) ~ E/3 from SAWADA11 80 kPa, nu ~0.5

relaxation_s.src: SAWADA11 in vivo relaxation time 494 s (FE fit)

conductivity_W_mK.src: hydrated soft tissue ~0.5 (skin/muscle class); not measured for mucosa

effusivity.src: sqrt(k rho c) from the E values above

wet.src: ASSY23 film present at all intra-oral sites

dry.src: dry mouth / air-dried surface: BONGAERTS07 dried saliva mu 2-3 on model surfaces; tissue gloss drops to its own alpha

pressed.src: blanching under pressure as skin (skin.body pressed); threshold not measured for mucosa

ASSY23.cite: Assy Z, Jager DHJ, Brand HS, Bikker FJ. Salivary film thickness and MUC5B levels at various intra-oral surfaces. Clin Oral Investig 27:859-869 (2023)
ASSY23.lic: open access, licence not checked; numbers used as facts (via MTT R22)

CHOI20.cite: Choi JJE, Zwirner J, Ramani RS, et al. Mechanical properties of human oral mucosa tissues are site dependent. Clin Exp Dent Res 6:602-611 (2020); Thiel-embalmed, 2 male donors 69/81 y, uniaxial tension 20 mm/min, 22 C

SAWADA11.cite: Sawada A, Wakabayashi N, Ona M, Suzuki T. Viscoelasticity of human oral mucosa: implications for masticatory biomechanics. J Dent Res 90:590-595 (2011); in vivo indentation + FE fit
SAWADA11.lic: paywalled; abstract numbers used as facts

KYDD67.cite: Kydd WL, Mandley J. The stiffness of palatal mucoperiosteum. J Prosthet Dent 18:116-121 (1967), as quoted in CHOI20

BONGAERTS07.cite: Bongaerts JHH, Rossetti D, Stokes JR. The lubricating properties of human whole saliva. Tribol Lett 27:277-287 (2007); PDMS ball-on-disc
BONGAERTS07.lic: paywalled; abstract numbers used as facts

RANC06.cite: Ranc H, Elkhyat A, Servais C, et al. Friction coefficient and wettability of oral mucosal tissue: changes induced by a salivary layer. Colloids Surf A 276:155-161 (2006); piglet tongue

PRINZ07.cite: Prinz JF, de Wijk RA, Huntjens L. Load dependency of the coefficient of friction of oral mucosa. Food Hydrocolloids 21:402-408 (2007); mucosa-on-mucosa, 0.34-2.20 N, 0.1-700 mm/s
PRINZ07.lic: paywalled; abstract trends only (values not retrieved)

ANDABLO20.cite: Andablo-Reyes E, Bryant M, Neville A, et al. 3D biomimetic tongue-emulating surfaces for tribological applications. ACS Appl Mater Interfaces 12:49371-49385 (2020); PVS/alginate impressions of 15 adults' tongues

HO15.cite: Ho DK, Ghinea R, Herrera LJ, Angelov N, Paravina RD. Color range and color distribution of healthy human gingiva. Sci Rep 5:18498 (2015)

JACQ13.cite: Jacques SL. Optical properties of biological tissues: a review. Phys Med Biol 58:R37-R61 (2013): soft tissue n 1.36-1.40, g 0.8-0.95
JACQ13.lic: paywalled; numbers used as facts (via skin.body / chromophores.json)

WATER.cite: engine/materials/profiles/water.json (saliva variant: SCHIPPER07 viscosity, ERMPS18 surface tension, n 1.335 E)

MTT.cite: the project's research note mouth_teeth_tongue.md (project research file, 2026-10-19; its R-numbers name the primary papers)
MTT.lic: project file; the numbers it carries are facts from the cited papers
